synopsis: The braking system must work across rain, snow, fog, dust, dusk, darkness and glare, but coverage cannot be assumed to transfer between different sites, machines and weather combinations [f285, f3599, f614]. The planned mid-2027-plus-four-month validation window falls in northern summer and autumn, excluding natural snow, freezing fog and low winter sun; winter 2026–2027 is the last cold-season collection opportunity before that window [f11943, f10461]. Start existing warning-fleet sensor recording in October 2026 and continue through winter, capturing raw sensors, machine buses and environmental metadata; preferentially selecting good-weather, daytime recordings would bias coverage [f97, f728, f5661]. Weather chambers, generated dust, fog and rain, southern-hemisphere sites and winter fleet recordings can partly mitigate the seasonal shortfall, but proving grounds cannot control weather or establish natural exposure, dust remains the biggest off-road sensor-simulation gap, and no accepted simulated-weather realism score exists [f777, f5729, f11949, f11950]. The proposed coverage strata already exceed 7,000 cells, statistical demonstration of off-road weather generalisation remains unresolved, and expert judgment rejects a newcomer delivering a fully credible all-weather toolchain by mid-2027 [f5468, f2879, f1590].
